title: Policy Sandbox: Scenario-Driven Console Editor for Region/Tier Selection & Fallback Tuning
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a policy sandbox within the Console that lets customers author and validate region selection, tier routing, and fallback model-variant rules using realistic traffic scenarios. The editor must be WYSIWYG with a scenario runner that shows latency/cost/quality tradeoffs and highlights unsafe rules. Scope: editor surface, scenario builder, validation linter, simulated previews for single requests and traffic slices, and an exportable policy JSON schema. Out of scope for this ticket: server-side policy enforcement, billing integration, and full A/B rollout automation (follow-ups planned).
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create a policy with region priorities + tier weights + fallback variants in the Console editor

Scenario runner accepts synthetic or uploaded traffic (CSV) and simulates routing results with per-step telemetry: selected region, tier, model variant, expected latency percentile, and token cost estimate
Validation linter surfaces safety/compatibility issues (missing fallback, circular priorities, incompatible model capability) with clear fix suggestions
Preview pane shows at least three visualization modes: timeline for request traces, heatmap for region/tier selection frequency, and a cost vs latency scatter for simulated requests
Editor exports a validated policy JSON that conforms to runtime schema and includes a generated policy summary for customer support
risks: Simulated metrics may diverge from production under bursty workloads. The scenario runner must avoid giving false confidence; include prominent caveats and tie to canary guidance. Engineering cost to support CSV uploads and large simulation sets may push backend effort beyond the estimate.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy editor in feature-flagged Console for internal customers; 2) Run closed-beta with three pilot customers (week-long tests); 3) Collect feedback, tune validation rules, then gradually enable for all self-serve accounts. Provide 'preview-only' mode for orgs using Private deployments.
notes: Design: prefer a three-column layout (composer, scenario runner, preview). UX tradeoff: inline suggestions vs side-channel explanations — initial MVP will use inline linter bubbles with a docs link for advanced reasoning. Implementation will re-use the existing policy JSON schema and the simulation engine built during ENG-19234.
